content.title: About
content.content: Cooked fennel bulb is the edible swollen stem base of Foeniculum vulgare, a staple in Mediterranean cuisine. Heat softens its texture and brings out a sweet, anise‑like flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fennel belongs to the Apiaceae family, along with dill and carrots.
The seeds are used as a spice, while the bulb is treated as a vegetable.
References to fennel appear in ancient Greek medical texts.
Fennel essential oil is used in aromatherapy and perfumery.
In some cultures, cooked fennel is served as a light post‑surgical diet.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Fennel provides quercetin and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber and volatile oils stimulate bile flow and relieve gas.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie nutrient source
items.content: A cup of cooked fennel is low in calories yet supplies potassium, magnesium, and several vitamins.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, and fiber can lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as rash or swelling.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Fennel essential oil can enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for users of blood thinners.

items.title: Thyroid concerns
items.content: Large amounts of raw fennel seeds contain goitrogens that may affect thyroid function.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked fennel can be served warm as a side dish, added to salads, soups, and stews. It may be roasted, braised, or simply boiled until tender, then seasoned with olive oil, lemon, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fennel in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze the pieces on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag; they retain quality for up to 2 months.
